properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. A sub-question of `dec:idea-does-reflow2-ship-design-principles-to-every-project` — the guard matched it and it is deliberately separate, because that one asks WHETHER to ship and this asks a question that has to be answered even after "yes", and answers to it are what make the difference between options there.

THE COLLISION. Anthony's framing was "advisory guidelines ... of course the user can waive them". Reasonable, and it runs straight into `dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking` (2026-08-08, accepted): **`enforced` has THREE states and NO default** — `true`, `false`, and ABSENT meaning nobody has said. The default was REMOVED on purpose, because a convention recorded in passing used to assert it could fail somebody's build; that is how all four of reflow2's own enforced rules got that way, not one of them chosen.

So each way of shipping answers the enforcement question differently, and none is free:

(A) SHIP THEM `enforced: false`. Matches his words. BUT it is reflow2 asserting a policy about consequence in a project it knows nothing about — and consequence (whose build stops, who is blocked at 2am) is exactly what that decision says is the USER'S to state. A team that would want "no silent fallbacks" to stop their build is told by an unchosen default that it does not.

(B) SHIP THEM WITH `enforced` ABSENT. Honest by that decision's own lights. BUT `unstated_rule_enforcement` fires at 0.4 per rule, so a freshly-genesised project starts life owing SEVEN gaps it did nothing to earn — a gap list greeting you on day one, which is the "list that gets skimmed" failure the acknowledge tools exist to prevent, arriving at the worst possible moment.

(C) ASK AT ADOPTION. The starter pack is offered, and adopting a principle IS answering its enforcement question, one at a time, in the user's own words. Nothing is asserted and no gap is manufactured. COST: seven questions at genesis, the moment a user has least context and most to do — and the governance-proposal skill's own warning applies, that asking about a fourth rule in one session turns the asking into noise people wave through.

(D) SHIP ADVISORY, MAKE THE WAIVER THE RECORDED ACT. Default `false`; a project that wants one enforced says so. Inverts (A)'s problem rather than solving it: cheap for the common case, still an unchosen answer in the graph.

⚠️ A FOURTH QUESTION HIDES UNDER ALL OF THEM: an ENFORCED rule owes a DETECTOR (`unverified_enforced_rule`, 0.6, until a PASSING check exists). Several of these principles are judgements no detector can compute — "was this the root cause?" is the one just met head-on in `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap`, which Anthony ruled ADVISORY on exactly that ground. So a shipped principle set would arrive carrying reflow2's own open question `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all`, which may make that requirement a PREREQUISITE for shipping principles rather than a neighbour of it.

⭐ THE ONE THING THAT SEEMS SETTLED WHICHEVER WAY THIS GOES: whatever ships must record that a project ADOPTED or WAIVED a principle, because a waiver nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from never having heard of it — the same shape as the patch nobody wrote down in `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, one layer up.
properties.name: OPEN — "advisory by default" is itself a default asserting something, and `enforced` was deliberately given no default; how does a shipped principle answer that question honestly?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. "Advisory by default" sounds free and is not: dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking deliberately removed the default, because whether breaking a rule stops a build is a claim about consequence only the user can make. Every option either asserts that answer, manufactures seven day-one gaps, or spends seven questions at the moment the user has least context.
